Material 
Processing 
Hot Working Practices – Wrought materials shall have a minimum total hot work 
reduction ration of 4.0:1. 
One of the following two process sequences shall be used. 
Process One 
Process Two 
1) Basic electric furnace (EF). 
2) Either argon oxygen decarburization 
(AOD) or vacuum oxygen 
decarburization (VOD). 
3) Vacuum arc remelting (VAR).

1) Vacuum induction melting (VIM).
2) Either Electroslag remelting (ESR), 
electroflux remelting (EFR) or VAR. 
3) Optional step ESR, EFR or VAR. 
Grain Size: The average grain size shall be determined in accordance with ASTM E112 
for unimodal distribution or ASTM E1181 for random duplex grain size distribution. The 
ASTM average grain size shall be No. 2 or finer. 
In the case of random duplex grain size bimodal condition each area fraction average 
grain size numbers reported shall be No. 2 or ﬁner. 
No topologically duplex grain size, as defined and measured per ASTM E1181, is 
allowed.

Solution annealed and aged hardened. Ultrasonic Inspection Capability per Cactus 
Wellhead Nondestructive Specification CNT-005 – Ultrasonic Testing

Equipment 
Equipment Qualification and Calibration 
Heat treatment operations shall be performed with heat-treating equipment that 
satisfies one of the following: 
 
Calibrated in accordance with API 6A section 6.5.2 and 6.5.3 and surveyed in 
accordance with API 6A Annex M and section 6.5.4.1 for batch type furnaces, 
or 
 
Equipment has been calibrated and surveyed in accordance with SAE AMS 
2750 Class 1, 2 or 3 for tempering and Class 1, 2, 3, 4 or 5 for normalizing and 
austenitizing. 
Heat treatment operations shall be performed utilizing equipment qualified in accordance 
with API Specification 6A including Annex M. Furnace instrumentation shall be calibrated 
at least every 3 months with acceptable grace period as defined in SAE AMS2750. 
Furnaces shall be surveyed no less than once a year. When a furnace is moved, repaired 
or rebuilt refer to SAE AMS2750 for survey requirements. 
Temperature Monitoring 
The material temperature shall be measured by use of either a contact surface 
thermocouple or a heat sink. 
The hold time shall not commence until the contact surface thermocouple, or a heat sink 
reaches at least the minimum required material temperature. 
If a heat sink is used it shall be made of the same class of material. The ER of the heat sink 
shall be greater than or equal to the largest ER of any single part in a heat treatment load.

Microstructural 
Analysis 
 
Sample(s) shall be from material with the same shape and equivalent round (ER) 
from each remelt ingot per heat treat lot and shall be subjected to a 
microstructural analysis. Where heat treat lot is material from the same remelt 
ingot; processed together using the same procedures and hot/cold work 
equipment; same nominal dimensions (excluding length); and heat treated in the 
same furnace loads, including solution annealing, aging and, if applicable, re-heat 
treatment. The sample shall be either a prolongation (full cross-section on thickest 
end) or sacrificial production part. 
 
The sample(s) to be examined shall be a minimum ¼ in (6 mm) square and oriented 
longitudinally to the primary axis of grain flow. If the cross-section of the material 
is less than ¼ in (6 mm), then the sample(s) shall be full cross-section. The 
microstructural analysis shall be performed on material in the final heat treatment 
condition. Test locations shall be a minimum of 1.25 in. (32 mm) from a heattreated end surface. 
 
For solid material, the center, 1/4 thickness and surface locations shall be 
evaluated. For hollow material, the mid-wall location and both the inner and outer 
surfaces shall be evaluated. 
 
The material manufacturer or material supplier shall retain the metallographic 
specimen mounts for 5 years minimum following the date of the examination. 
 
The acceptable etchants are for microstructural examination are shown below:

a Etchants shall be made, used, and stored in accordance with their documented useful life. 
b Milliliters (ml) should be used as the standard unit for ratio parts. 
Metallographic Examination for Deleterious Phases: The microstructural samples 
shall be examined for deleterious phases. The microstructural samples shall be 
examined at 100X and 500X using light microscopy. 
Acceptance criteria are as follows: 
a) The microstructure for all alloys shall be free from acicular phases except in 
individual, isolated grains that are not representative of the bulk 
microstructure. In no case shall any individual grain be surrounded with 
acicular phases.
Cactus Wellhead Material Specification

Microstructural 
Analysis 
b) The microstructures shall be free from continuous networks of secondary 
phases along grain boundaries, except for individual, isolated grains or isolated 
fields of view (0.008 in (0.203 mm) x 0.010 in (0.254 mm) area of the 
microstructure representative of the area shown in a 4 in (102 mm) x 5 in (127 
mm) photomicrograph taken at 500X) that are not representative of the bulk 
microstructure. The presence of discrete, isolated particles of secondary 
phases or carbides is acceptable. 
c) There shall be no Laves phase. (Examination of the microstructural samples for 
Laves phase is not required if the final melt source certifies that the material is 
free from Laves phase.) 
Examples of acceptable and unacceptable microstructures photomicrographs can be 
found in API Standard 6ACRA, Annex A, Figure A.1 through Figure A.20. 
Material that is rejected for unacceptable microstructural features may be fully re-heat 
treated (solution annealed, and age hardened) in accordance with this CMS and reexamined. 
If a heat treat lot is rejected, then the other pieces within the heat treat lot may be 
qualified on an individual piece basis if both ends are examined and meet the 
microstructural requirements. 
Tensile Property 
Requirements 
 
One tensile test shall be performed for each tested QTC. The test frequency shall 
be one test per remelt ingot per heat treat lot 
 
The QTC shall be either a prolongation (full cross-section on thickest end) or 
sacrificial production part. 
 
For solid material the test specimen shall be, a standard size (0.500 in. or 12.5 mm 
gage diameter) round specimen with a gage length with minimum of four times 
gage diameter (4D) shall be used unless the product size or geometry does not 
permit for machining of such a specimen and for such cases the largest sub-size 
round specimen (4D minimum) possible shall be used. 
 
For hollow material either largest sub-size round specimen (4D minimum) or strip 
specimen shall be used. Strip test specimens are only permitted on hollow material 
up to 0.750 in. (19 mm) wall thickness. 
 
The test specimen and test method shall be in accordance with ASTM A370 or 
ASTM E8. Rounding of test results to determine conformance to specification shall 
be in accordance with ASTM E29. 
 
The tensile properties shall meet the acceptance criteria of this CMS. 
 
 If the results of the tensile test(s) do not satisfy the applicable requirements, two 
additional tests on two additional specimens (removed from the same QTC with no 
additional heat treatment) may be performed to qualify the material. The results of 
each of these tests shall satisfy the applicable requirements.
Cactus Wellhead Material Specification

Charpy 
Requirements 
 
Charpy V-notch impact testing shall be performed on all material in accordance 
with ASTM A370 or ASTM E23. All tests shall be performed at or below -75 °F (-60 
°C) regardless of API 6A temperature classification. 
 
The QTC shall be either a prolongation (full cross-section on thickest end) or 
sacrificial production part. 
 
For solid material, the test specimens shall be removed from a location at 1/4 
thickness or deeper from the side or outer diameter and at least 1.25 in. (32 mm) 
from the end. For hollow material, the test specimens shall be removed from a 
mid-wall location from the side and at least 1.25 in. (32 mm) from the end. 
 
The test specimens and test method shall be in accordance with ASTM A370. 
Rounding of test results to determine conformance to specification shall be in 
accordance with ASTM E29. 
 
Impact testing shall be performed on a set of three specimens. Specimens oriented 
transverse to the primary direction of grain flow shall be used unless the size or 
geometry of the QTC prevents the usage of transverse specimens (material less 
than 3 in. [76 mm] in cross-section). For transverse specimens, the orientation shall 
be either C-L or T-L and for longitudinal specimens, the orientation shall be either 
L-C or L-T. See ASTM E1823 for specimen orientation. 
 
One set of Charpy V-notch impact tests shall be performed for each tested QTC. 
The test frequency shall be one set of tests per heat per remelt ingot per heat treat 
lot 
 
The average energy value for a set of three specimens shall meet or exceed the 
specified average listed above. No more than one of the specimens shall have an 
energy value below the specified average and it shall not be below the specified 
single minimum. No specimens shall have a lateral expansion below the specified 
value. 
 
If sub-size samples are used the adjustment factors for the sub-size impact 
specimens below shall apply to the absorbed energy values for all product 
specification levels (PSLs). Lateral expansion shall be as stated above regardless of 
specimen size.

 
The hardness tests shall meet the acceptance criteria shown in the Mechanical 
Property section of this CMS. 
 
Rounding of test results to determine conformance to specification shall be in 
accordance with ASTM E29. 
Production Material Testing 
Each piece of production material shall be hardness tested on or near the surface using 
the Rockwell C scale method per ASTM E18 or ASTM E110, or the Brinell (10 mm ball, 
3000 kgf) method per ASTM E10 or ASTM E110 after the final heat treatment cycle. The 
surface may be prepared using light grinding. When light grinding is used it shall be to a 
maximum depth of 0.125 in. (3.18 mm). 
 
Alternatively, for each piece of production material, near surface hardness 
testing on a cross-section shall be acceptable. Near surface test shall be 0.100 
to 0.150 in. (2.54 mm to 3.81 mm) from the surface and shall be performed 
using the Rockwell C scale method per ASTM E18. 
 
For Rockwell C-scale testing, three adjacent indentations shall be made, 
averaged to calculate the mean, and the mean shall meet the hardness limit of 
this CMS. No individual hardness number may be greater than 2 HRC units 
above the maximum specified hardness number. For Brinell testing, one 
indentation is sufficient. 
 
If any Rockwell hardness requirements are not met, three additional Rockwell 
C scale indentations shall be made in the immediate area to determine new 
hardness numbers. If any Brinell hardness requirements are not met, two 
additional Brinell tests may be taken in the immediate area. If one or more of 
the re-test indentations do not meet hardness requirements of this CMS, then 
the piece is rejected. 
Qualification Test Coupon (QTC) Testing 
The QTC shall be either a prolongation (full cross-section on thickest end) or sacrificial 
production part. 
 
Cross-section hardness testing shall be performed on each QTC using the 
Rockwell C scale method per ASTM E18 or ASTM E110. For solid material, the 
center, 1/4 thickness and near surface locations shall be evaluated. For hollow 
material, the mid-wall location and both near the inner and outer surfaces shall 
be evaluated. At each location three adjacent indentations shall be performed, 
and the mean hardness number from each location shall meet the 
requirements listed above. The hardness test location for the near surface test 
shall be 0.100 - 0.150 in. (2.54 mm - 3.81 mm) from the surface. All hardness 
indentations shall be reported. No individual hardness indentation may be 
greater than 2 HRC units above the maximum specified hardness number. 
 
If any mean (average) hardness value does not meet requirements, a retest 
may be made by taking three additional indentations in the immediate area of 
the same location. Each new indentation shall meet the hardness 
requirements. The test specimen surface may be re-grounded before 
performing retesting. Only one re-grind and retest is allowed for each 
specimen. 
 
If one or more of the indentations do not meet hardness requirements of this 
CMS, then the piece is rejected.
Cactus Wellhead Material Specification

Conversions
Requirements on conversion and reporting of hardness measurements is listed below. 
In case of dispute, the Rockwell C scale shall be the referee method and shall take 
precedence. 
 
The conversion of hardness readings to or from other scales is material 
dependent. The Rockwell C scale is the preferred hardness method for 
hardness testing the family of alloys covered by API 6ACRA since compliance 
with ANSI/NACE MR0175 is frequently required and ANSI/NACE MR0175 
specifies the maximum acceptable hardness limits using the Rockwell C scale. 
When conversions from other hardness scales to the Rockwell C scale are 
required or vice versa, one of two methods shall be used: 
o A hardness conversion based on the formula in Annex C of API 6ACRA. 
(See table below) 
o A hardness conversion agreed to by the equipment manufacturer and

Conformance 
A Certification of Compliance (COC) shall be provided. 
 
The COC shall state that the supplier certifies that the raw material has been tested 
and complies with the terms of the Cactus Wellhead Purchase Order and this CMS. 
 
The topological duplex grain size testing was performed according to this CMS. 
 
The material complies with the requirements of the metallographic examination 
for deleterious phases according to this CMS. 
 
The certificate shall be validated by an authorized supplier representative, 
independent of the manufacturing operations.
